full_text_en:
Sanhe Trade Co., Ltd. v. Ping An Insurance Co., Ltd., Nanning Office
— dispute over insurance contract for waterway transportation of goods

Plaintiff: Sanhe Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Dongfeng Road, Qinzhou City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Yang Ruisheng, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Tang Yun, attorney at Haiwan Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Song Jie, attorney at Guoxing Law Firm.

Defendant: Ping An Insurance Company of China, Ltd., Nanning Office, domiciled at: Qixing Road, Nanning City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
Responsible Person: Huan Linsheng, Director of the Office.
Agent ad litem: Fan Shu'an, attorney at Xingchen Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Chen Dong, attorney at Xingchen Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Sanhe Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Sanhe Company"), filed an action with the Nanning Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region against the defendant, Ping An Insurance Company of China, Ltd., Nanning Office (hereinafter "Insurance Office"), concerning a dispute over an insurance contract for waterway transportation of goods. The Nanning Intermediate People's Court transferred the case to the Beihai Maritime Court for trial.

Plaintiff's Allegations: After the goods insured by the defendant for the plaintiff were lost, the defendant failed to assume insurance liability in accordance with the insurance agreement. Following numerous claims by the plaintiff, the defendant entered into two new agreements with the plaintiff on April 15, 1997, and April 22, 1997, respectively, stipulating that, on the basis of paying the plaintiff RMB 900,000, the defendant would gradually make up the full insurance proceeds for the goods carried by the vessel "Lian Ji 56". However, the defendant failed to perform as agreed. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to pay insurance proceeds of RMB 729,711.32 and investigation expenses of RMB 40,000, as well as liquidated damages of RMB 251,750.41.

Defendant's Defense: The plaintiff, Sanhe Company, could not prove that it had an insurable interest in the goods carried by the vessel "Lian Ji 56"; therefore, the insurance contract concluded between the parties should be null and void. Moreover, the plaintiff was clearly negligent in finding a qualified carrier, resulting in the fraud by the vessel "Lian Ji 56", and should bear the responsibility itself. The agreements signed between the parties on April 15, 1997, and April 22, 1997, concerning their insurance relationship, were a settlement agreement for the "Lian Ji 56" claim, and the defendant had already performed the agreement. The "Lian Ji 56" claim was thus settled, and the plaintiff had no further right to claim compensation from the defendant. The insurance compensation paid by the defendant to the plaintiff on July 7, 1997, was for another entirely unrelated claim, and the plaintiff's characterization of it as supplementary compensation for the goods carried by the "Lian Ji 56" was baseless. The court should dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

Facts Found by the Court (Beihai Maritime Court):

On May 21, 1996, the plaintiff, Sanhe Company, entered into a waterway transportation goods insurance agreement with the defendant, the Insurance Office, for the transportation of 10,000 tons of raw sugar owned by the plaintiff. The agreement stipulated: the insured amount was 110% of the total cargo value; the coverage conditions were All Risks; the insurance period was warehouse to warehouse; the goods to be carried were to be shipped in batches; the specific insured amount was to be determined based on the vessel information and loading capacity provided by the shipping company; Sanhe Company would provide a list in due course. In the event of a claim, Sanhe Company should promptly provide relevant documents, and the Insurance Office would complete compensation to Sanhe Company within 20 days after determining the amount of loss. After the insurance agreement was signed, to complete the transportation of the goods, Sanhe Company, through Fangchenggang, chartered 19 vessels, including the "Lian Ji 56", to carry the 10,000 tons of raw sugar. The Insurance Office issued cargo transportation insurance policies, confirming the insured amount and premium amount for the goods carried by each vessel.

On May 31, 1996, the plaintiff, Sanhe Company, entered into a voyage charter party with the Shanghai Freight Service Company of the Shishi Shipping Company of Fujian Province, agreeing that the vessel "Lian Ji 56" would carry 450 tons of raw sugar. On the same day, the goods were loaded on board, and the Fangchenggang Port Authority, on behalf of the vessel "Lian Ji 56", issued a waterway cargo waybill (No. 96044) with Sanhe Company as the shipper and Guangzhou Huaqiao Sugar Refinery as the consignee; the defendant, the Insurance Office, also issued a cargo transportation insurance policy (No. GX00B0031960000015, hereinafter "Policy No. 015"). The policy stated: means of conveyance "Lian Ji 56" vessel; departure date May 31, 1996; port of loading Fangchenggang; port of destination Guangzhou Huaqiao Sugar Refinery; insured cargo: raw sugar, 450 tons; coverage conditions: All Risks; insured amount: RMB 1,642,500; waybill No. 96044. On June 4, 1996, Sanhe Company paid the Insurance Office the premium under Policy No. 015 in the amount of RMB 4,927.50.

On June 1, 1996, the vessel "Lian Ji 56", loaded with the plaintiff Sanhe Company's 450 tons of raw sugar, departed from Fangchenggang, but had not arrived at the destination port by June 10, 1996. Sanhe Company promptly notified the defendant, the Insurance Office, and reported the matter to the Fangchenggang Public Security Bureau and the Harbor Supervisory Authority, incurring investigation expenses of RMB 40,000. On June 20, 1996, Sanhe Company submitted a claim to the Insurance Office and provided relevant evidence. Subsequently, despite numerous claims by Sanhe Company, the Insurance Office refused to settle on the grounds that Sanhe Company had been defrauded by the vessel "Lian Ji 56" and had failed to fulfill its duty of disclosure. Finally, on April 22, 1997, after negotiations, Sanhe Company and the Insurance Office reached a "Settlement Agreement for Cargo Damage under Policy No. 015" concerning the cargo damage of raw sugar on the "Lian Ji 56". The agreement stipulated: with the consent of both parties, the Insurance Office would make a one-time payment of RMB 900,000 to Sanhe Company to close the case; Sanhe Company would transfer its right to claim for the cargo damage to the Insurance Office. On the same day, the Insurance Office paid RMB 900,000 to Sanhe Company.

Prior to this, on April 15, 1997, the plaintiff, Sanhe Company, had also signed an "Import and Export Cargo Transportation Insurance Agreement" with the defendant, the Insurance Office, stipulating: Sanhe Company agreed to place transportation insurance with the Insurance Office for its import and export cargo; the specific type of coverage would be determined according to letters of credit or Sanhe Company's requests; the scope of liability for each type of coverage would be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the relevant import and export cargo insurance clauses; upon arrival of each batch of goods at the destination, regardless of whether a claim was made, the Insurance Office would refund 50% of the premium to Sanhe Company; this agreement would take effect from the date of signing and remain in force until Sanhe Company's losses were fully compensated. Pursuant to this agreement, the Insurance Office refunded 50% of the premiums paid, i.e., RMB 103,624.86, to Sanhe Company on July 7, 1997. Thereafter, Sanhe Company requested the Insurance Office to continue paying the remaining insurance proceeds for the cargo damage on the "Lian Ji 56", but the request was refused.

The above facts are confirmed by: agreements, insurance endorsement slips, insurance policies, premium receipts, the Settlement Agreement for Cargo Damage under Policy No. 015, insurance payment vouchers, premium refund vouchers, departure clearance report sheets, correspondence, claim applications submitted by the plaintiff Sanhe Company; waterway cargo waybills, cargo delivery lists, insurance payment vouchers, the Import and Export Cargo Transportation Insurance Agreement, voyage charter parties, correspondence submitted by the defendant Insurance Office; and the trial transcript. All evidence, having been subject to cross-examination by the parties and authentication by the collegial panel, serves as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

Opinion of the Court (Beihai Maritime Court):

Article 11 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "An applicant for insurance shall have an insurable interest in the subject matter insured. If the applicant does not have an insurable interest in the subject matter insured, the insurance contract shall be null and void. An insurable interest means an interest in the subject matter insured that is legally recognized. The subject matter insured means property and related interests, or the life or body of a person, that are the subject of insurance." The 450 tons of raw sugar insured by the plaintiff Sanhe Company with the defendant Insurance Office and carried by the vessel "Lian Ji 56" were owned by Sanhe Company. This ownership is an interest of Sanhe Company recognized by law; therefore, Sanhe Company had an insurable interest in the subject matter insured, the 450 tons of raw sugar. Article 85 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A contract is an agreement between parties to establish, modify, or terminate a civil relationship. A contract established in accordance with the law shall be protected by law." The insurance agreement signed on May 21, 1996, between Sanhe Company and the Insurance Office, with Sanhe Company's raw sugar as the subject matter insured, and the insurance policy issued by the Insurance Office to Sanhe Company on May 31 of that year, were both true expressions of the parties' intent on an equal and voluntary basis, and their content did not violate national laws; therefore, they were lawful and valid. The insurance contract relationship formed between the parties regarding these 450 tons of raw sugar was binding on both parties. The Insurance Office's defense that the insurance contract was null and void because Sanhe Company lacked an insurable interest in the subject matter insured was untenable.

All procedures for the plaintiff Sanhe Company's consignment of raw sugar were handled through Fangchenggang. Entrusted by Sanhe Company, Fangchenggang arranged for the vessel "Lian Ji 56" and issued the waybill on its behalf. This series of operations was normal procedure for waterway cargo transportation, with no indication of malicious collusion between Sanhe Company and the shipowner or insurance fraud. The disappearance of the vessel "Lian Ji 56" after carrying Sanhe Company's raw sugar could be due to various reasons, including possible fraud by the vessel against Sanhe Company, or the vessel possibly sinking at sea. For Sanhe Company, these were external factors causing the loss of the insured goods. Neither the law nor the provisions of the insurance contract signed between the parties stipulate or agree that the insured bears any responsibility for finding a vessel, or that the insurer can be exempted from liability if the insured is defrauded by the shipowner. It is precisely because of the numerous risks inherent in maritime transportation that an insured has the need to seek insurance from an insurer, and the insurance industry arises and develops. The disappearance of the vessel "Lian Ji 56" was not due to Sanhe Company's fault, nor was it foreseeable by Sanhe Company. Therefore, the defendant Insurance Office's defense that Sanhe Company was negligent in finding a carrier and that it should not bear insurance liability was also untenable.

The disappearance of the vessel "Lian Ji 56" after loading the goods resulted in an accident to the goods insured by the plaintiff Sanhe Company, indicating that an insured event had objectively occurred, and it fell within the scope of All Risks coverage underwritten by the defendant Insurance Office. Therefore, the Insurance Office should pay insurance proceeds in accordance with the contract.

The issue lies in the "Settlement Agreement for Cargo Damage under Policy No. 015" signed by the plaintiff Sanhe Company and the defendant Insurance Office on April 22, 1997. This agreement was voluntarily entered into by both parties, with clear expressions of intent, and its content did not violate national laws. Although the amount of compensation agreed upon in the April 22 agreement was far less than what Sanhe Company should have received after the insured event, because the agreement was a voluntary expression of Sanhe Company's intent and was a settlement agreement for the cargo damage under Policy No. 015, it should be regarded as a modification of the original compensation agreement under Policy No. 015. Article 13 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Parties shall have the right to dispose of their civil rights and litigation rights within the scope prescribed by law." The April 22 agreement signed by both parties was Sanhe Company's disposition of its own civil rights, which is permitted by law, lawful, and valid, and should be binding on both parties.

Prior to this, the parties signed an agreement on April 15, 1997, stipulating: "Upon arrival of each batch of goods at the destination, regardless of whether a claim is made, the defendant Insurance Office shall refund 50% of the premium to the plaintiff Sanhe Company; this agreement shall take effect from the date of signing and remain in force until Sanhe Company's losses are fully compensated." Since this agreement was signed before the April 22 agreement, and the April 22 agreement was a settlement agreement for the cargo damage under Policy No. 015, based on the legal principle that a later agreement prevails over an earlier one and a new contract prevails over an old one, it cannot be concluded that there is a necessary connection between the April 15 agreement and the April 22 agreement.

By entering into the April 22 agreement with the defendant Insurance Office, the plaintiff Sanhe Company terminated the insurance agreement signed on May 21, 1996, between the parties, waived its right to claim full insurance proceeds under Policy No. 015, and released the Insurance Office from its full liability to pay insurance proceeds under Policy No. 015. The Insurance Office's defense that the claim settlement for the goods carried by the vessel "Lian Ji 56" had been concluded was well-founded.

In summary, the Beihai Maritime Court rendered judgment on December 22, 1999:

The plaintiff's claims were dismissed.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 20,203 was to be borne by the plaintiff Sanhe Company.

The plaintiff Sanhe Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, stating: 1. The insurance agreement signed on May 21, 1996, and the insurance policy issued on May 31, 1996, were lawful and valid, and the appellee Insurance Office should pay the appellant full insurance proceeds of RMB 803,125.19, investigation expenses of RMB 40,000, and liquidated damages of RMB 353,375.08. 2. The "Agreement" signed on April 15, 1997, and the "Settlement Agreement for Cargo Damage under Policy No. 015" signed on April 22, 1997, violated the law, were obviously unfair, and were null and void; they should be revoked. Moreover, the appellee had refunded a premium of RMB 103,624.86 on July 7, 1997, pursuant to the April 15 agreement, which constituted a denial of the validity of the April 22 settlement agreement by conduct, indicating the appellee's willingness to perform obligations under the April 15 agreement. The appellant requested the court of second instance to uphold the appellant's lawful rights.

The appellee Insurance Office argued in its defense: The agreement signed on April 15, 1997, violated Article 105(4) of the Insurance Law, which provides that "Insurance companies and their staff members shall not promise to give insurance premium rebates or other benefits not provided for in the insurance contract to the applicant, the insured, or the beneficiary," and therefore was null and void. The settlement agreement signed on April 22, 1997, did not have any statutory grounds for invalidity and was a valid contract. There was a qualitative difference between the two agreements. The appellee's performance of the invalid April 15 agreement on July 7, 1997, could not be construed as denying the valid contract signed on April 22. The judgment of first instance was correct and should be upheld.

Upon further trial, the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region found that the appellant Sanhe Company had filed the first-instance action with the court on June 15, 1999. Otherwise, the court of second instance confirmed all facts found by the court of first instance.

The High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region held:

The insurance agreement signed on May 21, 1996, between the appellant Sanhe Company and the appellee Insurance Office was valid, as the parties had legal capacity, the expression of intent was true and lawful, and it should be a valid contract. After the occurrence of the insured event, the insurer should bear insurance liability pursuant to this contract. To resolve the insurance dispute, the parties subsequently signed two agreements on April 15, 1997, and April 22, 1997. The April 22 agreement stipulated that the insurance dispute concerning cargo damage under Policy No. 015 would be concluded on the condition that the Insurance Office paid Sanhe Company RMB 900,000 and Sanhe Company transferred its right to claim for the cargo damage to the Insurance Office. This agreement was a mutual expression of intent reached by the parties through consultation, did not violate national laws, and did not harm the interests of others; therefore, it should be a valid contract. This contract modified the insurance contract signed on May 21, 1996, and both parties should abide by it. Sanhe Company's request to rescind the agreement on the ground of obvious unfairness, made two years after the April 22 agreement had been performed and the insurance dispute arising from the cargo damage under Policy No. 015 had been closed, exceeded the one-year statute of limitations prescribed in Article 73(2) of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) and was not entitled to protection under law.

Since the April 22, 1997, agreement was signed after the April 15, 1997, agreement, and the April 22 agreement made no reference whatsoever to the April 15 agreement, even though the appellee Insurance Office performed the April 15 agreement on July 7, 1997, it could not be inferred that both parties had mutually agreed to override the April 22 settlement agreement. The appellant Sanhe Company's argument that the April 22 agreement had been denied was untenable.

In summary, the High People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region held that the judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and appropriate substantive disposition, and should be upheld. Therefore, pursuant to Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered judgment on June 6, 2000:

The appeal was dismissed, and the judgment of first instance was affirmed.

The appellate case acceptance fee of RMB 20,203 was to be borne by the appellant Sanhe Company.
